name: htmlparser2
input_api: new Parser(handler, {xmlMode: true}).write(string) then end(), after strict UTF-8 TextDecoder of local bytes; handler callbacks onopentagname, onattribute, onclosetag, ontext, oncdatastart, oncomment/oncommentend, onprocessinginstruction, onerror
license_evidence: package/LICENSE in the pinned npm tarball (MIT)
scope: One UTF-8 local document through htmlparser2's xmlMode callback events: raw qualified element and attribute names (prefix:local, no namespace URIs), attribute order and decoded values, xmlns/xmlns:* as ordinary attributes, decoded text and CDATA, comments, processing instructions including the XML declaration, CDATA count, tree depth; no DOCTYPE
family: htmlparser2 forgiving HTML/XML tokenizer (own Tokenizer.js state machine) with entities decode trees
family_note: htmlparser2 has its own Tokenizer and Parser; it shares no code with sax, saxes, @xmldom/xmldom, fast-xml-parser or libxml2. In xmlMode it switches the entities decoder to the XML decode tree, keeps tag case, recognizes CDATA and self-closing tags, and disables HTML implied open/close rules. It neither resolves namespaces nor enforces XML 1.0 well-formedness, so this is an XML-tolerant tokenizer path, not an XML 1.0 + Namespaces parser.

popularity.limitation: Package-wide npm downloads. htmlparser2 is mostly an HTML parser (default mode, and the parser under cheerio, domutils users and many HTML tooling chains); the count does not measure xmlMode use or XML parsing and must not be read as XML adoption.

oracle: projects/xml/javascript/htmlparser2/oracle.py (Python expat without namespace processing, ordered attributes, raw XML declaration via DefaultHandlerExpand)
verification_note: Measured as a raw-name XML event path, not as a namespace-aware XML parser. htmlparser2 returns qualified names only, so prefixes, local names, attribute order and xmlns declarations are compared as raw qualified-name strings; no namespace URI, expanded name or in-scope binding is produced by the parser or inferred by the harness. The comparison oracle is expat in non-namespace mode, which exposes the same fields. Fields htmlparser2 exposes but the oracle cannot (attribute quote style, startIndex/endIndex) are not compared.
